papers.title: Tunnel field-effect transistors exhibiting performance beyond the Boltzmann thermionic limit
papers.abstract: The International Roadmap for Devices and Systems (IRDS) has identified the tunnel field-effect transistor (TFET) as the most promising next-generation logic device that enables sustainable downscaling in driving voltage and power consumption. Demonstrating an acceptable sub–Boltzmann-limit ON current (namely I 60 , the current level when a TFET switches to a subthreshold swing level of 60 millivolts per decade) and current-switching ratio has presented a formidable challenge. We report a TFET based on a bismuth/indium selenide (Bi/InSe) heterostructure that exhibits an I 60 of up to ~10 microamperes per micrometer and a current-switching ratio of >10 7 . We attribute such promising TFETs to precise material design, clean interfaces fabricated under vacuum, and band engineering based on subthreshold swing physics. Our results demonstrate a high-performance basic building block that meets the IRDS requirements for next-generation integrated circuits.

papers.title: A tripartite genetic conflict system controls hybrid sterility in rice
papers.abstract: Interspecific Asian–African hybrid rice could substantially boost yield but is limited by severe hybrid sterility. We identify RHS3 as a major quantitative trait locus controlling this trait. RHS3 encodes a tripartite toxin–antidote system composed of MAO, DUN, and JIA, in which MAO acts as a toxin that aborts gametes by disrupting mitochondrial function, whereas DUN and JIA function as antidotes that neutralize MAO toxicity, conferring a transmission advantage to the African allele. We demonstrate that detoxification relies on selective autophagy through formation of a tripartite JIA–DUN–MAO protein complex. We infer the de novo origin of RHS3 in the AA-genome rice lineage, illustrating a role for genetic conflict in speciation and suggesting strategies to harness heterosis between Asian and African rice.

papers.title: High-efficiency, long-lived lead-free perovskite light-emitting diodes
papers.abstract: Tin halide perovskite light-emitting diodes (PeLEDs) offer promise due to their solution processability and low toxicity, yet low efficiency and poor stability hinder practical use. We found that electroluminescence failure in CsSnI 3 is primarily driven by excessive hole injection–triggered electrochemical Sn 2+ oxidation and an irreversible phase transition to Cs 2 SnI 6 . Through a dual-side optimization strategy combining formamidine doping with triphenylphosphine oxide modification to stabilize the perovskite lattice, suppress nonradiative recombination, and balance carrier transport, we demonstrate highly efficient near-infrared PeLEDs. These lead-free devices achieve a peak external quantum efficiency of 21.2% at 963 nanometers and a maximum radiance of 195.8 watts per steradian per square meter (W sr −1 m −2 ). Notably, the operating half-lifetime reaches 920.5 hours at 7.1 W sr −1 m −2 , providing pathways for high-performance lead-free PeLEDs.

papers.title: Genomic predisposition is associated with the direction of sex chromosome evolution
papers.abstract: Sex chromosome evolution is among the most dynamic genomic innovations in vertebrates, yet why some lineages evolve XY while others evolve ZW remains unclear. Using chromosome-level genomes from 19 geckos, we found that gecko sex chromosomes originated independently from 16 ancestral chromosomes. Their origins are nonrandom in both time and direction. Five of 11 datable origins coincide near the Middle Miocene Climatic Transition (~10 million years ago). Ancestral gene content is associated with the direction of evolution, with testis-enriched regions tending to evolve into ZW and testis-depleted regions into XY, a pattern observed across multiple amniote sex chromosome origins. Geckos with genetic sex determination repeatedly evolve partial dosage balance through up-regulation in the heterogametic sex. Sex chromosome evolution thus follows constraints from ancestral genomic predisposition and environmental context.

Autism mutations rewire protein interaction networks to drive neurodevelopmental pathology
papers.abstract: Systematic mapping of protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks and determining how causal mutations rewire them in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) provide a powerful framework for uncovering disease mechanisms and therapeutic opportunities. Using affinity purification–mass spectrometry, we systematically mapped PPIs for 100 high-confidence ASD genes, uncovering more than 1800 interactions. By assessing the impact of pathogenic missense mutations, leveraging AlphaFold, and validating key findings in human-derived model systems, we identified marked convergence onto shared protein complexes in the wild-type state and convergent PPI rewiring driven by independent mutations. For example, distinct patient-derived variants in FOXP1 disrupt its interactions with FOXP4, leading to changes in cortical neurogenesis and neural activity in brain organoids. Overall, these findings link genetic variation to protein networks and convergent neurodevelopmental dysfunction in ASD.

papers.title: Direct evaporation of single-crystal metal contacts for 2D semiconductors
papers.abstract: Metal contacts remain one of the key bottlenecks in two-dimensional (2D) semiconductor electronics. We developed an atomic-scale step-by-step evaporation method to directly grow single-crystal metals on monolayer semiconductors with clean interfaces. This method accesses a distinct growth-kinetic window that suppresses secondary nucleation and promotes lateral coalescence, enabling van der Waals epitaxy of diverse metals—including bismuth, silver, indium, gold, and palladium—on molybdenum disulfide (MoS 2 ) and tungsten diselenide (WSe 2 ). The single-crystal metals support ultrathin conduction, provide spatially uniform work functions, and exhibit improved thermal robustness. As contacts, they show minimal Fermi-level pinning, approaching the Schottky–Mott limit. With bismuth and palladium contacts, monolayer MoS 2 and WSe 2 transistors achieved ultralow n- and p-type contact resistances of 36 and 145 ohm-micrometers, respectively, and short-channel currents both above 1.1 milliampere per micrometer.

papers.title: Thermal cycling–induced nitriding increases energy-storage density in titanate ferroelectric films
papers.abstract: Enhancing dielectric energy-storage density ( U e ) requires maximizing the difference between maximum and remanent polarizations (Δ P ). Improving Δ P remains fundamentally challenging, as existing strategies rarely achieve simultaneous high maximum polarization and low remanent polarization. We introduce a postsynthesis treatment method, cryogenic thermal cycling, in which liquid nitrogen infiltrates the film and then is rapidly cycled to 100°C. This process markedly increases Δ P to 105 microcoulombs per square centimeter in oxide ferroelectric titanate films through oxygen vacancy–mediated nitrogen hybridization. Using this approach, we increased U e to 261 joules per cubic centimeter with an efficiency approaching 80%. This approach is broadly applicable to diverse film materials with thicknesses spanning the nano- to microscale, offering a facile and cost-effective route to overcoming the critical bottleneck in Δ P and U e .

papers.title: Recent strengthening of eastern Pacific ENSO in the last millennium paleorecord
papers.abstract: The Pacific El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) generates climate extremes that endanger ecosystems, infrastructure, and human well-being worldwide. The response of this system to climate warming is poorly constrained, due both to data scarcity and uncertainties in climate models. The geochemistry of Galápagos coral skeletons across the past millennium reveals a large recent increase in interannual variability of sea surface temperature in the eastern equatorial Pacific compared to existing paleorecords that exceeds simulated natural variability. This increase parallels rising global temperature and results from stronger El Niño events. Central Pacific coral data also show increased variability, although less distinctly than in the Galápagos. Our results provide long-term context for understanding ENSO variability trends, with troubling implications for climate extremes.

The skill premium across countries in the era of industrial robots and artificial intelligence
papers.abstract: How do new technologies affect economic growth and the skill premium? To answer this question, we analyze the impacts of industrial robots and artificial intelligence (AI) across 52 countries using counterfactual simulations. In so doing, we simulate the nested CES production function framework of Bloom et al. (2025) with low-skilled workers, high-skilled workers, traditional capital, robots, and AI. Our contribution lies in documenting substantial heterogeneity across income groups: the inequality-increasing effect of robots and the inequality-reducing effect of AI are particularly strong in high-income countries, while they are less pronounced among upper-middle and lower-middle income countries. In addition, we show that both technologies boost economic growth. In terms of policy recommendations, our framework suggests i) balanced investment in both types of automation technologies to increase economic growth while keeping wage inequality subdued, and ii) investments in education and skill-upgrading to mitigate negative effects of robot use on wage inequality.

papers.abstract: Abstract We study a macroprudential regulation in the emerging market of Chile that raised loan-loss provisions for residential mortgages with loan-to-value (LTV) ratios above 80%. The policy reduced high-LTV borrowing and overall leverage but unintentionally affected households likely to borrow above 80% LTV based on preregulation characteristics. These borrowers liquidated term deposits to meet higher down payments, lowering liquidity and raising short-term delinquency, especially near the threshold. The results uncover a regulatory trade-off: systemic risk is curbed, but financially constrained households face short-term vulnerability. (JEL G21, G28, D40)

papers.title: Droughts and borrowing patterns in poor countries: Evidence from Tanzania
papers.abstract: This paper examines whether and to what extent droughts reshape household borrowing patterns in fragmented credit markets in developing economies. Using nationally representative household panel data from the two most recent waves (2014/15 and 2020/21) in Tanzania combined with drought indicators, we analyse borrowing responses across lender types – banks, microfinance institutions, and informal lenders – and across credit purposes – business, non-food consumption, and subsistence expenditures. Tanzania is used as a representative case of sub-Saharan African economies that share three institutional features: fragmented credit markets with a dominant informal lending sector, rain-fed agricultural livelihoods exposed to drought risk, and low financial inclusion. The paper reports three findings. First, droughts do not increase borrowing from banks and microfinance institutions but significantly increase borrowing from informal lenders. Second, drought-induced credit is directed at subsistence rather than productive recovery. Third, we examine three mechanisms that may explain these patterns: financial inclusion, credit tightening, and drought-caused crop failures. Results show that households farther from bank branches and mobile money agents significantly increase informal borrowing during droughts. For credit tightening, we find no significant borrowing response from formal lenders, and in some cases, a decline in formal borrowing. Results also show that households experiencing drought-induced crop failures significantly increase subsistence borrowing. These results reconceptualise climate-shock credit response in fragmented financial markets, demonstrating that droughts can reallocate borrowing across market segments and loan purposes.

papers.title: Impact of the Collection Mode on Salaried Labour Income Data: Evidence From Colombia Before and During the COVID ‐19 Pandemic
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The strict confinement implemented by the National Government of Colombia in 2020 to contain the expansion of the COVID‐19 pandemic created challenges in data collection operations conducted through household surveys. As a result, surveys that traditionally relied on face‐to‐face collection methods transitioned to a remote mode using telephone surveys. We exploit a quasi‐experimental design based on the geographical‐temporal exogenous variation in the collection mode of the leading household survey for the Colombian labour market and the linkage of this survey to the nationwide social security administrative record to measure the impact of the change in the collection mode on the reported salaried labour income. We find that the change in collection mode reduces the measured salaried labour income by approximately 4.4 percentage points and increases its variance and dispersion, with differences between population groups. These findings have implications for the development of mixed data collection methods and the analysis of income‐based statistics.

papers.title: On Pasinetti’s “separation theorem” applied to money
papers.abstract: In his 2007 book Keynes and the Cambridge Keynesians. A ‘Revolution in Economics’ to be Accomplished, Luigi Pasinetti advocates a “separation theorem” which distinguishes between the “natural” level of “pure theory” and the “institutional” level of the study of “actual economies”. He mentions money as an area of analysis where some aspects are to be dealt with at both levels. The aim of the paper is at discussing how this “separation theorem” may apply to money. It is shown that, in Pasinetti’s model of a monetary “pure labour production economy”: 1) The number of “degrees of freedom” is actually two, not three as claimed in the book – a point acknowledged by Pasinetti in private correspondence; 2) The deleted degree of freedom reflects the absence of the medium of exchange function of money; 3) This absence may be remedied by reinterpreting the two degrees of freedom in the terms offered by Ricardo’s theory of money; and 4) This interpretation preserves Pasinetti’s analysis of debt and credit relations as part of a “natural distribution of income” and gives a consistent basis to the application of the “separation theorem” to money. An additional import of the paper is that it draws on a hitherto unpublished private correspondence on this matter with Luigi Pasinetti in 2012.
papers.journal_name: The European Journal of the History of Economic Thought

papers.title: The Missing Middle Managers: Labor Costs, Firm Structure, and Development
Screening Adaptive Cartels
Prime Locations
papers.abstract: We develop a method for delineating prime locations—ultradense clusters of economic activity—within cities and apply it to comprehensive establishment data covering all US metropolitan areas. We further use big data to extend the analysis to a global context where administrative data are sparse. Many cities in the United States and around the world are dominated by a small number of prime locations that can concentrate up to one-half of tradable services jobs on tiny shares of land and are dominant centers of economic gravity. In cities with fewer prime locations, a larger tradable services share concentrates in them. (JEL C55, R23, R32, R38, R52, R58)

papers.title: Unconditional Convergence in Manufacturing: A Reassessment
papers.abstract: The movement of labor out of agriculture is a central feature of the development process. A long-held view is that successful development requires that much of the labor released from agriculture be allocated to manufacturing rather than services. Rodrik's (2013) finding of unconditional convergence for manufacturing productivity, using data from UNIDO, provided empirical support for this view. We argue that the UNIDO data are ill-suited for studying cross-country productivity dynamics. Using recently released GGDC data designed for this purpose, we revisit the issue and find no evidence of unconditional convergence in manufacturing productivity over 1990–2018. (JEL D24, J24, L60, O13, O14, O47, Q10)

papers.title: What Is Newsworthy? Theory and Evidence
Pricing with Algorithms
papers.abstract: This paper studies Markov perfect equilibria in a repeated duopoly model where sellers choose algorithms. An algorithm is a mapping from the competitor's price to own price. Once set, the algorithms respond quickly. Customers arrive randomly and sellers can periodically revise their algorithms. The main results are that (i) for the simple two-price model with standard profit functions, monopoly pricing is the unique equilibrium outcome, and (ii) for general finite price grids, all equilibrium outcomes feature supra-competitive pricing. Sustenance of such collusion seems outside the scope of current antitrust laws for it does not involve any direct communication.

papers.title: How Test-Optional Policies in College Admissions Disproportionately Harm High-Achieving Applicants from Disadvantaged Backgrounds
The Missing Loan-to-Value Cycle
papers.abstract: We show that the equilibrium loan-to-value (LTV) distribution in the US mortgage market has been remarkably stable over the last quarter century, both in aggregate and region by region, despite large, cross-sectionally heterogeneous house price cycles. While high-LTV mortgages changed from being explicitly government backed to privately securitized and back, their overall fraction remained unchanged. A repeat-sales methodology and an analysis of loan performance confirm that this stability in the distribution of LTVs holds even within subgroups of the population. These findings are inconsistent with models of credit cycles that use changes in collateral constraints to generate boom-and-bust dynamics in house prices. (JEL C43, E32, G21, G51, R21, R31)

papers.title: Correction: The world is your office: how work from anywhere boosts talent, productivity and innovation
Does Anti-Tax Avoidance Regulation Curb Industry Concentration?
Disintermediation Governance and Complementor Innovation: An Empirical Look at Amazon.com
papers.abstract: This study investigates how the platform’s disintermediation governance policy (i.e., the policy that disciplines complementors and consumers circumventing the platform to transact directly) affects complementors’ product innovation and launching strategies. We leverage a change in the Communication Guideline on Amazon.com (i.e., the focal platform), which prohibits complementors (i.e., sellers) from sending external website links, telephone numbers, and email addresses to buyers in direct messaging, as a policy shock to Amazon complementors. By conducting a difference-in-differences analysis, we find that the governance policy significantly reduces product innovation on the focal platform among complementors with direct selling channels as measured by the number of new products and the innovativeness of new products. These main effects are mitigated by complementor reputation on Amazon and complementor multihoming. Mechanism analyses show that complementors with direct selling channels increase the number of new products launched through those channels after the policy change (i.e., the switching effect). Moreover, complementors tend to strategically switch innovative and high-value products away from the focal platform while leaving less innovative but price-competitive products on it to attract Amazon consumers before diverting to their direct selling channels (i.e., the bait effect). Our results have implications for platform governance policies regarding disintermediation and its impact on complementor product innovation and launch strategies both on and off the focal platform. This paper was accepted by D. J. Wu, information systems. Funding: G. Gu gratefully acknowledges research support from the USC Marshall School of Business. Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2024.04439 .

papers.title: Surviving and changing the field: Navigating gendered contextual barriers of geosciences
papers.abstract: What does it take for a woman to thrive in an occupation that takes her to some of the most remote, rugged, and unforgiving locations on Earth? How do women geoscientists defy gendered barriers to succeed in an occupational context that requires both technical expertise and physical endurance? Using a social constructionist perspective, we examine the interplay of gendered barriers resulting from the physical and social context of such work, and women’s strategies to overcome them. We analyzed 67 semi-structured interviews with men and women geoscientists and, through the lens of context theorizing, uncovered a configuration of gendered barriers, both physical and social, the strategies employed by women to navigate those barriers, and the impact of organizational practices that perpetuate or address the gendered barriers. Women’s survival strategies to adapt to the context and organizational practices that supported adaptation often reinforced gendered barriers. Women’s change strategies and organizational practices that directly addressed the barriers were more effective.

papers.title: From Capital to Green Innovation: Corporate Venture Capital as a Vehicle for Sustainable Organizational Learning
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT As increasing stakeholder pressure pushes firms to embed sustainability into their strategies, this study explores how corporate venture capital (CVC), a key corporate entrepreneurship instrument, supports corporate parents to learn from sustainable startups. Based on organizational learning theory, we examine the CVC's role in facilitating knowledge transfers across CVC‐startup‐corporate‐triads. Using an inductive approach, we interviewed 38 CVC and 20 startup managers across Europe. We find that sustainability alters the learning process: evolving knowledge, multidirectional flows, and resource mobilization. Structured exchange, enablers, like trust‐building initiatives, and barriers, including intellectual property concerns or not‐invented‐here‐syndromes, shape this process. We synthesize our findings into a dynamic framework and nine CVC typologies based on sustainability orientation and strategic corporate alignment, consolidated into matchmakers and collaborators. Theoretically, we extend organizational learning and CVC literature by emphasizing that sustainability reshapes learning dynamics in kind. Practically, we offer guidance on structuring CVC programs to succeed in sustainability transformation.

papers.title: Beyond Awareness: Emotional and Physiological Reactions to Climate Terminology
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The terminology used to describe climate change has become increasingly contested in sustainability and organizational communication. However, existing research provides mixed evidence regarding the effectiveness of different climate‐related terms. This research shows that different climate‐related terms evoke distinct emotional and physiological reactions, which shape communication effectiveness. A key contribution of this research lies in disentangling conscious from automatic responses. Specifically, the article analyzes how more alarming climate terms ( climate crisis and climate catastrophe relative to the baseline term climate change ) elicit conscious responses in terms of verbalized emotions and reactance, as well as physiological responses in terms of arousal and visual attention. Two experiments were conducted. Using data from Germany, France, and the United Kingdom, Study 1 found that “climate catastrophe” provoked stronger negative emotions and higher reactance. Both positive and negative emotions boosted social media engagement, whereas reactance diminished it. Study 2 integrated electrodermal activity and eye‐tracking measures to capture automatic responses. Results showed that “climate catastrophe” intensified arousal and visual attention, but these responses did not translate into higher engagement. In sum, this research highlights that more alarming climate terminology can be a trigger for raising awareness. However, such terminology can also backfire, creating trade‐offs that organizations must consider when designing climate communication strategies.

papers.title: Unlocking the Relationship Between Corporate Environmental Performance and Financial Outcomes Under National Environmental Policy Framework: Panel Evidence From China
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines the relationship between corporate environmental performance (CEP) and corporate financial performance (CFP) under China's evolving environmental policy regime. Using a panel dataset of 1,312 Chinese A‐share listed firms from 2010 to 2023, we find a significant negative association between CEP and CFP. The findings challenge the assumption that improved CEP necessarily enhances financial outcomes and suggest that, in emerging markets, environmental improvement may impose short‐term financial burdens on firms. National environmental policies change the CEP–CFP relationship in heterogeneous ways, with some policies intensifying the negative association and others attenuating it. The financial consequences of CEP are context‐dependent and affected by policy design, regulatory enforcement, and the maturity of market‐based incentive mechanisms. Drawing on the cost–benefit perspective, institutional theory, stakeholder theory, and the resource‐based view, this study advances extant literature by highlighting that the CEP–CFP relationship is policy‐driven, offering implications for managers and policymakers.

papers.title: How do consumers react to unfair reviews? Examining the matching effects of review type and response strategy on purchase intentions
Toward a Theory of Dyadic Trust in Family Firms: How Kinship Complicates the Trajectory of Mutual Trust
papers.abstract: Mutual trust within workplace dyads is key to forging productive relationships and facilitating organizational success. Yet, we know little about the relationship factors that explain why some dyads develop and maintain mutual trust while other dyads fail to do so. This is particularly true in family firms, where dyadic kinship factors challenge implicit assumptions and theoretical tenets of trust research. Thus, we offer a novel, contextually grounded perspective on dyadic trust by theorizing how kinship complicates the trajectory of mutual trust in family firms. Our framework illuminates how family firms offer a unique and opportune context to extend trust research.

papers.title: Strategic adoption of additive manufacturing in edible product supply chains: a resource-based view on sustainability
papers.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how the strategic value of additive manufacturing (AM) is created in edible product supply chains, using the resource-based view (RBV) as a theoretical lens. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on 29 semi-structured interviews with experts from the food, pharmaceutical and AM sectors, this research refines an initial, literature-based conceptual model and develops an empirically grounded framework. Findings AM’s VRIN attributes are necessary but not sufficient for strategic value; value depends on deployment within supply chain configurations. Three pathways are identified: supply chain transformation, product innovation and operational improvement. SMEs integrate AM strategically, while large incumbents often contain it within R&D. Sustainability outcomes remain conditional on economic viability, which acts as a gatekeeper for environmental and social value. Practical implications The framework offers decision guidance for practitioners: SMEs are shown the organisational prerequisites for pursuing supply chain transformation through AM, while large firms are given concrete signals for when to migrate AM from R&D into core operations. Policy levers for lowering adoption barriers are also identified. Originality/value This study extends the RBV by revealing that resources generate competitive advantage through multiple independent pathways, and that organisational context determines resource strategic status, not merely moderating effectiveness but fundamentally shaping whether resources function strategically or operationally. It provides the first interview-based evidence of these dynamics in the previously underexamined context of edible product supply chains.
papers.journal_name: Supply Chain Management: An International Journal

papers.title: Customer evaluations of service failures by visibly physically disabled frontline employees: a mixed-method study
papers.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to examine how frontline employees’ (FLEs’) visible physical disability status influences customers’ stereotypes and subsequent loyalty. Drawing on the stereotype content model (SCM), we further examine how service failure type (process vs. outcome) moderates the effect of FLE disability status on customer stereotypes and whether communal relationships mediate the relationship between these stereotypes and customer loyalty. Design/methodology/approach A sequential mixed-methods approach is used. Semi-structured interviews with 105 customers informed a SCM-based framework, which was then tested through vignette-based experiments with 180 participants. Findings Compared to the no-failure condition, visibly physically disabled FLEs evoke higher perceptions of warmth under outcome-failure conditions, which in turn strengthen communal relationships and customer loyalty to the service provider. This effect is found to be insignificant in process failure relative to the no-failure condition. Research limitations/implications Theoretically, the study extends hospitality research by framing inclusive frontline design as a value-creating driver rather than merely an accessibility or compliance issue. It also shows that disability cues do not consistently mitigate customers’ responses to service failures; their effect depends on failure conditions and stereotypes. For practice, managers should design frontline roles for employees with visible physical disabilities around performance rather than stereotypes and address customer bias in encounters. Originality/value The study conceptualizes inclusive service design as a value-creation mechanism rather than merely an accessibility or compliance issue.
papers.journal_name: International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management

papers.title: From Advertisements to Ad Agents: A Relational Inference Framework for Agentic Advertising
papers.abstract: Advertising theory has traditionally conceptualized persuasion as arising from discrete persuasive exposures. Generative artificial intelligence challenges this assumption by enabling persistent, contingent, and perceptibly coordinated persuasion across interactions, platforms, and contexts. This article develops a relational inference framework for agentic advertising to explain how consumers organize recurring adaptive coordination into inferred ad agents that become the object of relational evaluation. The framework identifies three structural conditions for ad-agent emergence, specifies relational inference as the cognitive mechanism underlying that emergence, and proposes three complementary first-order relational judgments—artificial empathy, artificial recognition, and super-being social presence—that shape the second-order evaluations of authenticity and trust. It further explains how generative persuasion knowledge moderates these evaluations and identifies the recursive dynamics and boundary conditions of agentic advertising. By introducing inferred ad agents as a new unit of analysis, the framework extends exposure-centered advertising theory to continuously adaptive advertising environments.

papers.title: The effect of dynamic change in home-country institutions on emerging market firms’ speed of outward foreign direct investment
papers.abstract: Prior research on institutional dynamics has revealed the impact of institutional change on a firm’s internationalization decisions. We investigate institutional irregularity, which denotes the extremes of states of change in institutions. By integrating the dynamic institution-based view with the global factory framework, we examine the impact of COVID-19 institutions’ irregularity on the speed of an emerging market firm’s (EMF) first outward foreign direct investment (OFDI) after the pandemic’s outbreak, as well as the moderating effect of the EMF’s pre-pandemic OFDI scope. Our empirical tests of the first post-pandemic OFDI by EMFs reveal that home-country institutional irregularity accelerates firms’ post-pandemic OFDI, and that this effect is partially conditioned by the firm’s pre-pandemic OFDI scope.

papers.title: AI integration and cross-border knowledge sharing in MNEs' international marketing strategies: a systematic review and fact-based narrative perspective
papers.abstract: Purpose Artificial intelligence (AI) has become an essential driver of competitive positioning and advantage for multinational enterprises (MNEs). The integration of AI into marketing strategy has transformed how businesses interpret consumer behaviour, optimize campaigns and expand across international markets. We apply institutional theory and strategic choice theory to explore how strategic choice and institutional expectations create a continuous cycle of linked actions that lead to the development and reinforcement of AI integration patterns and practices within an organization, which also go on to underpin the change and transformation organizations have to go through. Design/methodology/approach Using a systematic literature review (SLR) of 156 research papers and a thematic and content analysis of 298 text units from industry-based literature – we synthesize the body of knowledge emerging from both to provide a comprehensive framework for understanding AI's role in the global marketing strategy structure of MNEs. Findings The findings from the SLR and fact-based narratives show convergence in collectively moving away from treating AI as a monolithic input and identifying the specific pathways through which AI-related capabilities shape organizational and market outcomes; reflecting a growing interest in sequential and mediated processes, as opposed to direct effects, suggesting that the value of AI in international and inter-organizational contexts is largely indirect and contingent on intermediate mechanisms such as knowledge digitization, cultural adaptation and dynamic capability development. Practical implications Managers must integrate risk assessments into AI strategy planning and diversify data infrastructure to mitigate over-dependence on politically sensitive regions. They must get into active scenario planning, AI adoption audits and stress-testing business models against plausible geopolitical disruptions. Organizations should weigh geopolitical risk into investment decisions and partnership evaluations from the outset. Originality/value This study integrates academic and industry insights to construct a cohesive framework for understanding AI's role in shaping global market competition. The findings show that MNEs have to develop twin capabilities, both institutional and strategic, to respond to external pressures and regulations. MNEs achieving success with AI integration are not merely viewing this as a technological upgrade, but as a key facilitator for reimagining their entire international marketing strategy structure, which creates agility for the organization to come up with market-responsive strategies in global operations. While mimetic isomorphic pressures encourage firms to adopt proven AI solutions, this does not preclude innovation and the differentiation in this context emerges not from whether MNEs adopt AI, but from with what institutional and strategic logic they deploy it.

papers.title: Understanding global social media influencer (SMI) marketing through credibility: a review, integrative framework and research agenda
papers.abstract: Purpose This research examines a globally relevant phenomenon of social media influencer (SMI) credibility through a systematic literature review (SLR) and develops a future research agenda. Design/methodology/approach The SLR of 155 articles on SMI credibility is conducted following the SPAR-4-SLR protocol and further organized using TCCM and ACM frameworks. Moreover, an integrative framework is conceptualized for a holistic view of influencer marketing. Findings The research reports findings per theories, characteristics (antecedents, consequences and moderators), contexts (countries, social media platforms and domains) and methods used in the literature. Moreover, the integrative framework depicts critical research themes: relationships, content, SMI characteristics and follower characteristics. A future research agenda is developed under each theme based on the gaps in the literature. Originality/value The article is the first to comprehensively define SMI credibility based on perceived believability and parasocial relationships. An integrative framework for a holistic view of SMI marketing is conceptualized, and a clear research agenda is developed under identified research themes.

papers.title: Perceived overqualification and work-family conflict: examining work-family centrality as a moderator
papers.abstract: The relationship between perceived overqualification and work-family conflict (WFC) is unclear. We argue that the extent to which it is either positive or negative depends on work-family centrality. Overqualified employees who prioritize work more than their families will appraise their jobs as failing to fulfill their needs for challenge and career development. This theorized needs-supplies misfit explains why perceived overqualification is positively associated with strain-based WFC through heightened career anxiety. Drawing on the demands-abilities fit perspective, we contend that overqualified employees possess greater capabilities than needed, resulting in a resource surplus that frees up capacity for family life. Accordingly, we propose that for employees who prioritize family over work, perceived overqualification is negatively related to time-based WFC through reduced work-role overload. Our hypotheses were supported across two studies (Study 1: a sample of 252 employees from a large Chinese banking group and their spouses; and Study 2: a time-lagged design with 280 employees from various industries). In Study 2, we also examined alternative mediators (i.e., anger toward employment situation and depressive symptoms), retested our model with behavior-based WFC, and demonstrated the construct validity of career anxiety. The study findings suggest that managers should consider overqualified workers’ work-family values to better manage their WFC.
papers.journal_name: The International Journal of Human Resource Management

papers.title: Organizational citizenship behavior (OCB)-informed performance evaluation: the role of organizational and cultural factors
Do brands need search advertising?
papers.abstract: Unlike traditional advertising, brands pay for search ads only if they are effective, measured by clicks. Clicks, however, are not sales. This paper presents results from nine field experiments conducted with eight small, direct-to-consumer (DTC) brands selling exclusively online with all sales captured in the dataset. Despite variations in brand, product category, and search advertising formats, stopping branded search advertising had no significant effect on sales for all eight brands. For two of three brands that stopped generic search advertising, there was a significant effect on sessions (website visits), but not sales. A pre-registered online experiment was also conducted, confirming the null effects of branded search advertising on sessions (measured as click intentions) found in the field experiments. These results indicate that brands should reallocate search-related marketing expenditure from branded to generic search ads, or search engine optimization to appear on the first results page.

papers.title: How Personal Pronouns Shape Persuasion
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Communication often involves personal pronouns. Consumers, for example, frequently say “ I love this restaurant” or “ you 'll enjoy those shoes.” How do first‐person (e.g., I) and second‐person (e.g., you) singular pronouns shape persuasion? Are communicators correct about which ones are more effective? Seven studies demonstrate an important misprediction. While communicators think that second‐person singular pronouns will be more persuasive, first‐person singular pronouns are actually more impactful. Further, the studies demonstrate the underlying mechanisms behind these effects. While communicators think second‐person singular pronouns will increase persuasion because they take the audience's perspective, second‐person singular pronouns actually reduce persuasion because they encourage reactance. These findings highlight the important impact of ubiquitous language features, deepen understanding around drivers of reactance, and have important implications for communicators who want to increase their impact.

papers.title: In Favor of Digital Detox: Developing the Attitude Toward Digital Detox Scale
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The extensive usage of digital devices can lead to technological overload, potentially damaging interpersonal relations, individual performance, and personal well‐being. Digital detox describes consumers' counter‐reaction by intentionally reducing the use of digital devices for a specific period of time. This research introduces the theoretical conceptualization and empirical development of the one‐factorial 7‐item Attitude toward Digital Detox (ADD) scale, which measures consumers’ favorable attitudes toward temporarily reducing digital consumption. Across seven studies, we attest to the strong psychometric properties of the scale, show its relation with related constructs (e.g., mindfulness, self‐control, implicit theories of intelligence), provide evidence of its predictive validity for the time consumers spend watching online videos, and demonstrate known‐groups validity based on both activity preferences (offline vs. online) of Reddit groups and lecture format preferences (in‐person vs. online) of students. Our scale enables future research on antecedents and consequences of the attitude toward temporarily reducing digital consumption.

papers.title: Hello, [Your Name]: Why Name‐Based Personalization Enhances Chatbot Effectiveness
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Organizations increasingly adopt chatbots as strategic tools to engage with consumers and strengthen brand outcomes. This study explores how chatbots that use name‐based personalization in their communications can more efficiently influence consumer behavior towards the brand. Across five experimental studies, we demonstrate that name‐based personalization within chatbot messages enhance perceptions of chatbot sincerity and brand sincerity, leading to more favorable consumer attitudes and higher purchase intentions toward the brand. The effect of personalization on perceived chatbot sincerity is mediated via perceived anthropomorphism. Further, we identify a few boundary conditions for the positive effects of name‐based personalization, namely chatbot performance and perceived overuse of name‐based personalization. These findings contribute to the literature on personalization, anthropomorphism, branding, and the Computers Are Social Actors (CASA) theory, and offer practical implications for marketers seeking to design effective chatbots for brands.

papers.title: How Loneliness, Trust, and Age Shape Evaluations of Human Versus AI‐Based Advisory Services
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Loneliness is becoming increasingly pervasive, a trend that also happens to coincide with the rapid growth in artificial intelligence (AI) systems that provide personalized recommendations for consumers. Across three experimental studies, we examine how loneliness impacts evaluations of advisory services using human or AI‐based guidance. In Study 1, lonely individuals report a greater willingness to pay (WTP) for a service that provides human‐based advice. Study 2 provides process evidence by showing that lonely individuals report greater trust in and subsequently greater WTP for a service that provides human versus AI‐based advice. Study 3 expands these findings to a broader sample and identifies age as a moderator. While lonely younger individuals positively evaluate a service that provides human‐based advice, lonely older adults favor a service that provides AI‐based advice, suggesting a reversal in consumer evaluations. Overall, these findings suggest that marketers and service designers should consider both age and loneliness when implementing AI technologies in customer‐facing experiences.

papers.title: Dignify: A Dignity-Based Conceptual Framework for Defining Consumer Vulnerability in Services
papers.abstract: Service research on mechanisms facilitating vulnerable consumers’ well-being and service outcomes through respecting and affirming human dignity is sparse. This study advances consumer vulnerability research by integrating philosophy, marketing, consumer psychology, medicine, and Transformative Service Research (TSR) to examine the role of dignity in service encounters. This research employed netnography to gather data from two large disability communities on Reddit, while the critical incident technique was used to collect data from Reddit and Facebook, thereby enhancing the results. The findings led to the development of Dignify , a dignity-based definition of vulnerability and conceptual framework, which centers dignity in consumer vulnerability. Dignify reveals how Humanization (dignity affirmation) and Dehumanization (dignity violation) behaviors, along with Structural Factors and Social Factors (dignity affirmation or violation contexts), shape consumer (physical, mental, psychological, social, and financial well-being) and service outcomes (trust, loyalty, switching intentions, service failures, and word-of-mouth/electronic word-of-mouth [WOM/eWOM]). Services (particularly TSR) and marketing can benefit greatly by incorporating dignity in vulnerability research, providing a distinctive framework for both conceptual and practical advancements.

papers.title: Navigating Cross-Border Healthcare under Structural Vulnerability: The Role of Cultural Health Capital
papers.abstract: This research examines how Hispanic women living in the US–Mexico borderlands coordinate household healthcare across two national service systems through the lens of cultural health capital (CHC). Drawing on multimethod ethnography using in-depth interviews, participant observation, and online diaries, we show how informants build and deploy navigational, social, familial, and linguistic capital to manage structural vulnerability in cross-border care. Findings demonstrate that women purposefully cultivate and allocate these forms of capital across three phases of healthcare shopping: pre-consumption, during shopping, and post-purchase. We identify consumer practices through which capital helps families navigate structural barriers, while also showing that such strategies emerge under conditions of constraint and do not eliminate exposure to risk. The study advances consumer vulnerability research by integrating structural vulnerability with CHC to theorize phase-specific capital orchestration and by specifying how intersecting vulnerability factors shape both exposure and response. We also translate these mechanisms into service design implications for providers, payers, and policymakers. In doing so, this research highlights the need for safer, more coordinated, and more culturally responsive care pathways that recognize the informal labor and cross-cultural expertise sustaining healthcare access in marginalized communities.

papers.title: A Temporal Perspective on Corporate Venture Capital Investments' Potential to Drive Innovation
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Corporate venture capital (CVC) investments are a major means by which corporations access information from startups to facilitate their own innovation. While the literature implies a static perspective, we offer a dynamic account that accommodates CVC investments' typical occurrence in staged rounds. Building on and adding to resource dependency theory, this study offers a research model that differentiates temporally between first and follow‐on CVC investments and their effects on the investing firm's product and business model innovations. Adding further temporal nuances, we also investigate whether the degree of relatedness between the investing firm's and the venture's industries affects these relationships. Using data on 708 firms from 2005 to 2019, we show that first CVC investments in new ventures particularly benefit investors' product innovations, while follow‐on CVC investments especially benefit their business model innovations. We also demonstrate that related investments tend to amplify the effects of first CVC investments, while unrelated investments tend to enhance the effects of follow‐on CVC investments. Thus, the study introduces a temporal perspective and highlights the complex interplay among the investment round, the type of innovation, and the relatedness of investments in determining CVC investments' temporal effects on innovation.

papers.title: Top management team stability and firm operational efficiency: a structural inertia perspective
papers.abstract: Purpose Drawing on structural inertia theory, this study aims to examine the relationship between top management team (TMT) stability and operational efficiency. It considers how TMT stability affects operational efficiency in terms of the balance between the benefits of consistent execution and the costs of constrained routine revision. Design/methodology/approach The conceptual framework is empirically tested using panel data on 3,289 Chinese listed firms from 2011–2022. Fixed-effects models are used for the main analyses, while 2SLS and a control function approach are adopted to help mitigate potential endogeneity concerns. Multiple robustness checks are also conducted. Findings The results reveal an inverted U-shaped relationship between TMT stability and operational efficiency. This curvilinear relationship varies across operating contexts, reaching its turning point at a significantly higher level of TMT stability when customer concentration is higher and at a marginally lower level when industry technological turbulence is higher. Practical implications The findings suggest that TMT stability can both benefit and constrain operational efficiency. Firms should therefore tailor their practices to the operating context, leveraging its execution advantages while mitigating its rigidity costs. Originality/value This study extends operations management research on the managerial antecedents of operational efficiency by introducing a structural perspective on TMT stability. It broadens TMT change research by focusing on the temporal continuity of the TMT. It also advances research on TMT stability and operational efficiency by identifying the operating conditions that shape their inverted U-shaped relationship.
papers.journal_name: International Journal of Operations & Production Management

papers.title: Corporate Political Contributions and (Ir)Responsibility: Lessons from India’s Political Finance Regime with Global Implications
Editorial Conflicts of Interest in Elite Peer Review
papers.abstract: Abstract The legitimacy of academic publishing depends on justified confidence in editorial integrity, yet the governance of elite journals often lacks accountability commensurate with its career- and field-shaping consequences. We audit 946 author–editor relationships across 788 articles published between 2010 and 2024 in two Financial Times 50 (FT50) journals and find widespread, patterned conflicts of interest (COI). Applying a conservative reasonable-observer standard, 49.7% of links involve at least one definitive COI and a further 11.6% are possibly conflicted, with prevalence increasing over time. COIs cluster within a small, dense, and homogeneous elite cohort of 54 highly prolific scholars, predominantly North American (90%) and male (94.5%), who account for roughly half of all publications. Reciprocal handling is most prevalent and embedded in hierarchical network structures, while editors within these networks exhibit disproportionate publication gains during service. A comparable non-FT50 journal shows substantially lower COI rates, largely attributable to the same elite cohort. These findings indicate that editorial COIs are systemic expressions of a collective-action problem rooted in institutional design, in which discretion and opacity enable recurrent insider advantage. Safeguarding legitimacy requires governance reforms that render editorial decisions transparent, enforce recusal, and enable systematic monitoring and accountability.

papers.title: From Language-Based Exclusion to Workplace Social Loafing Behavior: A Moderated–Mediation Model of Workplace Embitterment and Moral Attentiveness
An Empirical Study on the Driving Effect of Green Finance on Corporate Green Innovation Quality and Its Transmission Mechanism Under the Moderation of Financial Development Level
papers.abstract: This study examines how regional green finance affects corporate green innovation quality using panel data on 5,496 Chinese A-share listed firms from 2012 to 2023. Green innovation quality is measured by granted green invention patents, while a multidimensional green finance index is constructed using the entropy-weight method. Firm- and year-fixed-effects results show that green finance significantly improves green innovation quality, and the finding remains robust to alternative measures, lagged variables, sample adjustments, and instrumental-variable estimations. Mechanism analysis indicates that R&D investment partially transmits this effect. Financial development further strengthens the positive relationship. Heterogeneity tests confirm that the effect remains significant across firms with different technological status, overseas investment, ownership, and regional environmental regulation.

papers.title: Does Workforce Gender Diversity Influence Banks’ High-Level Decisions? Evidence on Credit Growth and Risk-Taking
papers.abstract: We investigate the impact of workforce gender diversity on the relationship between women’s representation in the board of directors and other decision-making bodies, and bank performance in credit growth. Using panel data on Turkish banks from 2006-2020, we find that while female directors and managers alone correlate negatively with credit growth, likely due to women being more risk-averse, there are positive synergies when the workforce composition is tilted towards women. The results suggest that female directors and managers are more effective in facilitating bank lending by lowering bank risk when there is greater workforce gender diversity, and higher representation of women in the workforce. This highlights the importance gender diversity and inclusion as an organizational value, manifested by the presence of women at all levels of the organization, in establishing a sound risk culture and compliance. Regulators may want to encourage diversity disclosure at all levels, not only in boards.

papers.title: How Does China Reshape the Global Technological Landscape?—An Analysis from the Identification, Spillover, and Institutional Drivers of Total Factor Productivity Leap
papers.abstract: Understanding how late-developing economies can transform from technology recipients into sources of technology spillovers remains an important yet underexplored question. Drawing on annual total factor productivity (TFP) data for China and 17 other G20 economies from 1978 to 2023, this paper applies time-varying econometric methods to trace the evolution of cross-country technology spillovers and to identify the institutional factors underlying China’s transformation. The results indicate that China has become a net source of TFP spillovers within the G20, with the reach of its spillovers expanding gradually from developing resource-based economies to advanced European and North American economies. This transformation was driven by two major nonlinear TFP leaps, both of which coincided with landmark institutional reforms. Furthermore, China’s outward spillovers to other G20 members have strengthened significantly since the mid-1990s, whereas the technological influence of developed economies on China has weakened over the same period. By documenting how a late-developing economy’s spillover role evolves across countries at different development stages, this study provides new evidence on the changing position of emerging economies in the global technology landscape and offers policy implications for late-developing economies seeking sustained productivity growth.

papers.title: Quantifying Cross-Border Risk Shocks to China’s New Energy Industry: Evidence from Frequency-Domain Networks and Interpretable Machine Learning
papers.abstract: This paper constructs a transnational industry-level risk network linking China’s new energy value chain with major developed-market industries to quantify cross-border risk shocks and examine their associated macroeconomic conditions. The results show that developed-market technology- and resource-related industries, including semiconductors, software, hardware, raw materials, and energy, are associated with substantial positive risk shocks to China’s new energy sector, whereas the automotive industry acts as a net risk receiver. Frequency-domain decomposition indicates that high-frequency spillovers dominate overall risk connectedness. Using interpretable machine learning, we find that international macroeconomic variables consistently possess stronger predictive power than domestic variables, accounting for approximately 75–85% of total feature importance. Furthermore, accumulated local effects analysis uncovers pronounced nonlinear threshold effects: (1) U.S. bond yields exhibit a U-shaped association with risk spillovers, turning sharply positive above approximately 2.8%; (2) VIX effects remain dormant below 30, after which predicted spillovers rise steadily; (3) global supply chain pressure activates an immediate positive marginal effect beyond zero; (4) trade policy uncertainty exerts a step-function impact even at low values, while economic policy uncertainty follows an S-shaped accumulation pattern. These findings offer key insights for strengthening China’s new energy supply chain resilience and risk management.

papers.title: Civil Servants and Democratic Backsliding: The Role of Managerial Signals
papers.abstract: Abstract Political efforts to weaken democratic institutions place civil servants in a dilemma between political responsiveness and protecting democratic values. As civil servants are embedded in the political-administrative hierarchy, we argue that signals from their direct hierarchical superiors are critical to understand how civil servants address this dilemma. Using a randomized survey experiment among Norwegian national-level civil servants (N = 1,446) and ordered logistic regression models, we find that democratic backsliding increases opposition to government wishes, internal and external voice, and consideration of exit from the organization. Managerial signals moderate these effects: civil servants are more inclined to voice concerns or consider exit when managers signal responsiveness to government wishes. In a conceptual replication and extension among US federal, state and local civil servants (N = 504) using ordered logistic regression models, we likewise find a greater inclination to exit if the manager signals responsiveness to government wishes, but also that respondents are less inclined to voice concerns to the manager. Overall, our findings imply that managerial signals within the political-administrative hierarchy are shaping civil servants’ immediate reactions to democratic backsliding.

Cooperative multi-EV aggregator strategy of V2G-enabled charging stations under shared interconnection limits
papers.abstract: The widespread adoption of electric vehicles creates new opportunities for energy management through vehicle-to-grid participation. When multiple electric vehicle aggregators operate behind a shared point of common coupling, uncoordinated scheduling can cause congestion and inefficient use of interconnection capacity. This paper addresses their coordination when schedules are coupled by shared grid limits and aggregate-dependent electricity prices. A key finding is that coordinated scheduling alone cannot sustain cooperation when cooperative gains are unevenly distributed. Settlement mechanisms guaranteeing individual rationality at aggregator and vehicle levels are therefore required for implementable coordination. Accordingly, a cooperative multi-aggregator scheduling framework is proposed for V2G-enabled charging stations under shared grid-connection limits and aggregate-dependent pricing. The scheduling model minimizes energy procurement costs and battery degradation penalties while enforcing shared import and export limits at the point of common coupling. Cooperative gains are allocated through a two-level asymmetric Nash bargaining mechanism that preserves the coordinated physical dispatch whenever EV-level settlement is feasible. Otherwise, the framework returns the business-as-usual outcome, ensuring individual rationality at aggregator and vehicle levels. A distributed alternating direction method of multipliers solution is developed to preserve EV-level privacy with limited inter-aggregator information exchange. Numerical results for 10-vehicle, two-EVA and 80-vehicle, four-EVA systems show cost reductions of 3.7% and 13.9%, respectively, relative to the uncoordinated benchmark, with no-worse-off outcomes. Robustness is confirmed under parameter variations, alternative bargaining weights, and stochastic EV-demand uncertainty. The results demonstrate the value of cooperative multi-EVA strategies in reducing costs while preserving grid-connection constraints and privacy.

papers.title: Institutional compression in climate policy integration: coordinating green electricity certificates and carbon emissions trading in China
papers.abstract: Coordinating market-based climate instruments is a central challenge for climate policy, yet the institutional mechanisms through which centralized governance systems pursue such integration remain insufficiently understood. This study examines how China coordinates Green Electricity Certificates (GEC) and Carbon Emissions Trading (CET), two instruments administered by separate bureaucracies. Drawing on 1,137 policy documents from 2017 to 2024 across 29 provinces, we combine BERTopic, cosine similarity analysis, and Bayesian Exponential Random Graph Models to trace central discourse convergence, provincial transmission heterogeneity, and horizontal coordination dynamics. Three findings emerge. First, central policy discourse shows rapid GEC-CET convergence after the 2020 carbon-neutrality pledge, with cross-referenced policy objectives rising from 7.3% to 18.6% within 24 months. This compressed trajectory contrasts with the more incremental development of the EU ETS, while also leaving important technical protocols, including double-counting safeguards, insufficiently specified. Second, provincial transmission exhibits persistent core–periphery gradients within the observation period: eastern provinces show high alignment with central policy discourse, whereas several western and resource-dependent provinces remain lower despite positive growth. Third, network reciprocity and transitive closure are positively associated with the formation of policy-integration ties alongside hierarchical policy-node effects and policy-tool covariates. Instrument associations are context-dependent: economic incentives are more strongly associated with integration in mature market settings, while capacity-building tools are more salient in regions with emerging institutional infrastructure. These findings contribute to climate policy integration research by showing how compressed institutional timelines, uneven local capacity, and horizontal network dynamics jointly shape coordination between market-based climate instruments, while highlighting implications for carbon-accounting readiness under the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism and regionally differentiated transition planning.

Knowledge graph-enhanced carbon impact assessment of construction and demolition waste with large language model-based decision support
papers.abstract: Construction and demolition waste sector generates substantial carbon emissions across sorting, transportation, and disposal phases. However, existing assessment approaches often generate static numerical results that offer limited traceability, regulatory interpretation, and decision-support capability. This study proposes an integrated framework that combines a knowledge graph with a large language model for construction and demolition waste carbon emission management. A domain-specific construction and demolition waste Carbon Knowledge Graph is constructed in Neo4j to integrate waste categories, treatment methods, facility information, source-referenced emission factors, and regulatory constraints. Carbon emissions from sorting, transportation, and disposal are quantified using an emission factor-based approach and embedded into the graph for traceable accounting. A retrieval-augmented generation mechanism connects the knowledge graph with a large language model, enabling natural language querying and evidence-based explanations. A residential demolition case study demonstrates the applicability of the framework. The results indicate that transportation is the dominant emission phase, accounting for 63.6% of total emissions, and show that the recycling-based pathway for concrete waste reduces emissions by 36.46% compared with the landfill-only baseline. This study contributes to bridging knowledge management and carbon modeling, providing an explainable, traceable, and regulation-aware decision-support approach for low-carbon construction and demolition waste management.
